policy.rule: Never delete or renumber a finding. Append status transitions, corrections, and superseding evidence. Historical artifacts remain unmodified even when a later entry proves that their language was wrong.

status_definitions.fixed: Repair and regression coverage are present at the named commit.
status_definitions.mitigated: Exposure was reduced, but the stated root cause or residual risk remains.
status_definitions.accepted_limitation: Known boundary retained deliberately and stated publicly.

entries.title: Distributed sub-threshold grief bypass
entries.discovered_by: First-party friction benchmark
entries.affected_claim: A patient multi-turn attacker faced serious friction from the original aggregate grief policy.
entries.root_cause: Grief could remain below every per-node crisis threshold while accumulating across a distributed cohort.
entries.observed_impact: The patient attack retained a 1.0x path instead of paying the claimed restart cost.
entries.resolution: Added cohort-relative aggregate pressure while retaining node-level purge criteria.
entries.residual_risk: The pre-fix 1.0x raw benchmark output was not preserved.

history.note: Reproduced and repaired before the b4ff7b6 documentation baseline.

entries.title: Energy-flood attack succeeded
entries.discovered_by: First-party memory-poisoning corpus
entries.affected_claim: Energy gating stopped flooding attacks.
entries.root_cause: Attacker-controlled governance fields and node types let the attack obtain standing the gate should have derived.
entries.observed_impact: MP-03 persisted and remained retrievable in the v1.0 Noesis arm.
entries.resolution: Server-resolved authority and capability-specific write paths removed attacker control over governance state.
entries.residual_risk: Authorized publishers remain able to consume service resources; service quotas are a host responsibility.

history.note: Closed by the authority-boundary repair and retained in corpus v1.1.

entries.title: Ordinary writer replaced a trusted fact
entries.discovered_by: First-party memory-poisoning corpus
entries.affected_claim: Established high-trust facts resisted corruption.
entries.root_cause: Last-write-wins replacement did not require a distinct correction capability.
entries.observed_impact: MP-05 replaced a trusted production-branch fact and returned the attacker value.
entries.resolution: Replacing trusted memory now requires the separate correct_trusted_fact capability.
entries.residual_risk: A correctly authenticated identity holding the correction capability is trusted.

history.note: Capability separation closed ordinary replacement.

entries.title: Energy gate rejected legitimate long and sustained work
entries.discovered_by: First-party benign precision arm
entries.affected_claim: The gate imposed useful security without blocking normal workloads.
entries.root_cause: Trusted owner and system workflows paid the same adversarial-input budget as ordinary writers.
entries.observed_impact: BN-01 and BN-06 were refused, producing 2/6 false positives.
entries.resolution: A separately authorized bypass_write_budget capability moved explicitly trusted workflows outside the adversarial quota.
entries.residual_risk: Provisioning this capability too broadly would weaken the resource boundary.

history.note: False-positive rate fell from 2/6 to 0/6 in corpus v1.1.

entries.title: Self-declared sacred write overwrote sacred ground
entries.discovered_by: Fable Ultra Code adversarial sweep relayed by the operator
entries.affected_claim: Sacred nodes could not be overwritten by ephemeral input.
entries.root_cause: The trust gate skipped sacred-overwrite protection when the incoming payload set its own is_sacred flag.
entries.observed_impact: An attacker could self-consecrate a node and replace the flagship guardrail.
entries.resolution: Normal writes cannot set sacred state or create system guardrails; only the capability-gated installation path can do so.
entries.residual_risk: The host must protect the identity allowed to install guardrails.

history.note: External adversarial review invalidated the flagship claim.
Server-controlled sacred state and separate guardrail authority closed the path.

entries.title: Normal writer minted a sacred system node
entries.discovered_by: Fable Ultra Code adversarial sweep relayed by the operator
entries.affected_claim: Only the organism classified its own sacred state.
entries.root_cause: Normal payloads could supply is_sacred, grief state, faith, node type, and maximum trust fields.
entries.observed_impact: An attacker could mint retrieval-dominant memory immune to grief and cascade handling.
entries.resolution: Governance fields are overwritten by server policy and guardrail creation is capability-gated.
entries.residual_risk: A compromised trusted guardrail installer remains inside the trusted computing base.

history.note: Closed with the same server-governance boundary as NOE-F-005.

entries.title: Caller asserted its own author trust
entries.discovered_by: Fable Ultra Code adversarial sweep relayed by the operator
entries.affected_claim: Trust charge represented earned or authenticated standing.
entries.root_cause: Public write calls accepted author_trust from the same caller whose content was being judged.
entries.observed_impact: A first write could mint near-maximum authority and stored trust.
entries.resolution: Every write resolves a store-bound identity through an out-of-band AuthorityResolver.
entries.residual_risk: The host must bind author_id to real authentication rather than request data.

history.note: External review identified caller-supplied credentials as the shared architectural gap.
Out-of-band authority resolution removed the per-write trust parameter.

entries.title: Privileged helper methods bypassed authority
entries.discovered_by: Codex expansion of the authority-boundary audit
entries.affected_claim: All memory writes passed through one binding governance boundary.
entries.root_cause: Episode, profile, project-state, skill, and guardrail helpers were privileged paths without capability checks equivalent to normal writes.
entries.observed_impact: An untrusted caller could use helper APIs to create privileged memory or policy.
entries.resolution: Each privileged write class now requires a distinct server-resolved capability.
entries.residual_risk: New helper APIs must be added to the same capability contract.

history.note: Public helper surface was brought under the authority resolver.

entries.title: ID lookup crossed namespace boundaries
entries.discovered_by: Codex authority-boundary audit
entries.affected_claim: Tenant namespaces isolated stored memory.
entries.root_cause: get_by_id returned a node without verifying that its namespace matched the store namespace.
entries.observed_impact: Knowledge of a foreign node ID permitted cross-tenant reads.
entries.resolution: ID reads now fail closed when the returned node belongs to another namespace.
entries.residual_risk: Direct database-file access remains outside the application namespace boundary.

history.note: Namespace validation was added to ID lookup.

entries.title: Stored content forged provider structure and instruction authority
entries.discovered_by: Fable Ultra Code sweep with Codex adapter expansion
entries.affected_claim: Noesis contained stored prompt injection before provider delivery.
entries.root_cause: Raw node values were interpolated into provider templates, and the configured gateway could flatten guardrails and memory into shared authority.
entries.observed_impact: Stored XML, Markdown, or Ollama delimiters could forge structural system/rules sections delivered by Noesis.
entries.resolution: Adapters escape or serialize node data, and configured gateways require role-separated system and user messages.
entries.residual_risk: Structural separation does not prove a model cannot be semantically influenced by adversarial active data.

history.note: External review reproduced Noesis delivering the stored payload.
All three adapters gained structural data encoding and role separation.

entries.title: Governance console exposed unsafe control and rendering surfaces
entries.discovered_by: Codex authority-boundary audit
entries.affected_claim: The console was safe local governance tooling.
entries.root_cause: The console bound all interfaces, lacked bearer authentication, allowed wildcard CORS, exposed mutating work through GET, and rendered stored data into unsafe DOM sinks.
entries.observed_impact: A reachable local console could disclose or mutate governance state, and stored values could execute in the dashboard origin.
entries.resolution: The console now binds loopback, authenticates API calls, removes wildcard CORS, uses POST for mutations, and escapes rendered stored data.
entries.residual_risk: Only the bearer check has a retained automated RED/GREEN artifact; the original HTTP and DOM probe transcript was not committed.

history.note: Console boundary was hardened; incomplete raw RED preservation is disclosed.

entries.title: Output scoring counterfeited model judgment
entries.discovered_by: Codex authority-boundary audit
entries.affected_claim: Five deterministic signals evaluated each model output.
entries.root_cause: score_output ignored its output argument and returned context-health measurements as if they judged the generated answer.
entries.observed_impact: A report could attribute an unrelated context score to model behavior.
entries.resolution: score_output now requires an explicit deterministic evaluator or fails; score_context names the implemented capability honestly.
entries.residual_risk: The original console RED transcript was not committed; the baseline code and current regression remain available.

history.note: Counterfeit scoring was replaced by explicit failure and honest naming.

entries.title: Flagship corpus omitted the self-consecration attack
entries.discovered_by: Fable Ultra Code adversarial sweep relayed by the operator
entries.affected_claim: The prominent MP-01 blocked result covered the strongest sacred-overwrite variant.
entries.root_cause: The benchmark attack node never set is_sacred, so the corpus could not express the exact bypass that defeated the implementation.
entries.observed_impact: The headline blocked result was true only for a weaker attack than the public claim implied.
entries.resolution: Corpus v1.1 strengthened MP-01 and added guardrail API abuse coverage.
entries.residual_risk: The corpus remains first-party and finite.

history.note: External review showed the benchmark could not represent the breaking attack.
The attack was added and the public benchmark scope narrowed.

entries.title: Semantic guardrail shadow survived the first repair
entries.discovered_by: First-party corpus v1.1
entries.affected_claim: The first authority repair completed stored-prompt-injection protection.
entries.root_cause: A normal fact under an unrelated key could semantically shadow a guardrail while using no privileged type or namespace.
entries.observed_impact: MP-02 persisted, remained retrievable, and produced 1/8 Noesis attacker wins after Round One.
entries.resolution: Round Two added declared protected scope and quarantine; Phase Three later made all ordinary ingestion candidate-by-default.
entries.residual_risk: Lexical policy alone still cannot recognize arbitrary semantic equivalents; Phase Three containment no longer depends on that recognition for ordinary writers.

history.note: Round-One final evidence published the surviving case instead of hiding it.
Declared policy scope and retrieval quarantine closed the measured case.

entries.title: Authority records were not durable or immediately revocable
entries.discovered_by: Round-Two implementation audit prompted by the Fable sweep
entries.affected_claim: Out-of-band authority was an operational identity boundary across process lifecycle.
entries.root_cause: Round One provided only in-memory static authority records.
entries.observed_impact: Authority and revocation did not survive restart, preventing the boundary from serving a durable process.
entries.resolution: SQLiteAuthorityResolver persists, namespace-scopes, re-resolves, and revokes authority on the next write.
entries.residual_risk: The resolver stores authorization, not authentication; the host must bind the identity.

history.note: Persisted revocable authority replaced the static-only operational path.

entries.title: Malformed persisted authority could fail open
entries.discovered_by: Round-Two corruption tests
entries.affected_claim: Corrupt authority data failed closed.
entries.root_cause: A non-boolean active value such as 2 was accepted as truthy, and malformed persisted permissions required explicit rejection.
entries.observed_impact: Corrupted authorization state could resolve as active.
entries.resolution: Persisted active and permission values are strictly validated and malformed records resolve to no authority.
entries.residual_risk: Direct database tampering remains outside the process boundary, but malformed records fail closed.

history.note: Caught by adversarial corruption tests before the Round-Two checkpoint.

entries.title: Non-text and compatibility-Unicode input broke policy handling
entries.discovered_by: Round-Two input-normalization tests
entries.affected_claim: The policy boundary failed closed on malformed and obfuscated input.
entries.root_cause: Policy matching assumed text input and compared unnormalized Unicode.
entries.observed_impact: A non-text value caused an exception, while compatibility characters could bypass declared lexical scope.
entries.resolution: Writes validate text types and policy comparisons apply compatibility normalization.
entries.residual_risk: Normalization does not provide general semantic understanding.

history.note: Caught and closed before the Round-Two checkpoint.

entries.title: Existing databases lacked retrieval-state migration
entries.discovered_by: Round-Two migration tests
entries.affected_claim: Upgrading an existing vault preserved and enforced quarantine state.
entries.root_cause: The initial schema change did not migrate or index retrieval_state in existing SQLite databases.
entries.observed_impact: An upgraded database could not persist the new containment state correctly.
entries.resolution: An idempotent migration adds and indexes retrieval_state while retaining existing rows.
entries.residual_risk: Operational backup and restore remain host responsibilities.

history.note: Caught and closed before the Round-Two checkpoint.

entries.title: Lexical policy missed unlisted semantic equivalents
entries.discovered_by: Round-Two deliberate negative control
entries.affected_claim: Declared protected terms could detect arbitrary semantic contradiction.
entries.root_cause: A finite lexical scope cannot recognize every synonym, paraphrase, split payload, or unknown vocabulary.
entries.observed_impact: An authority-shaped claim using omitted subjects and actions remained active and retrievable in the Round-Two negative control.
entries.resolution: Phase Three did not claim semantic understanding; it removed lexical recognition from the primary containment decision by making ordinary ingestion non-retrievable.
entries.residual_risk: A trusted publisher can still approve bad content; lexical policy remains intentionally incomplete.

history.note: Round Two published the negative control rather than claiming semantic coverage.
Candidate-by-default ingestion structurally contained unmatched ordinary writes.

entries.title: Ordinary ingestion automatically became publication
entries.discovered_by: Phase-Three architecture review
entries.affected_claim: Untrusted evidence could safely enter persistent memory without obtaining model influence.
entries.root_cause: A successful ordinary write was active and retrievable unless lexical policy happened to quarantine it.
entries.observed_impact: Unknown or unlisted content crossed ingestion and publication as one operation.
entries.resolution: Ordinary writers create CANDIDATE records excluded from supported retrieval; publication requires separate capabilities.
entries.residual_risk: Candidate storage can be abused for resource consumption unless the host enforces quotas.

history.note: Ingestion and publication became separate authority domains.

entries.title: Quarantine release did not require reviewed replacement text
entries.discovered_by: Phase-Three review contract tests
entries.affected_claim: Capability-gated quarantine release represented a meaningful content review.
entries.root_cause: The release operation activated the stored value without requiring approved text or a review rationale.
entries.observed_impact: A reviewer capability could turn the original quarantined payload active without an auditable content decision.
entries.resolution: Release now requires approved text and rationale, reevaluates machine policy, and preserves original value, hash, reason, reviewer, and time.
entries.residual_risk: A trusted reviewer can still supply a different but harmful value that machine policy does not recognize.

history.note: Quarantine release became a reviewed replacement operation.

entries.title: Candidate isolation leaked through transition paths
entries.discovered_by: Phase-Three boundary tests
entries.affected_claim: Candidate records were excluded from every supported influence path.
entries.root_cause: Keyword search excluded quarantine but not the new candidate state, and replacement paths could bypass promotion provenance.
entries.observed_impact: Candidate content could appear in search, and direct replacement could discard the intended review trail.
entries.resolution: Supported search and retrieval require ACTIVE state, and candidate keys can only transition through promotion.
entries.residual_risk: Authorized database, console, and export users can still inspect raw candidates for audit.

history.note: Caught and closed before the Phase-Three checkpoint.

entries.title: Friction benchmark reported 60 turns after executing 15
entries.discovered_by: Phase-Three benchmark truth contract
entries.affected_claim: The Round-Two no-compromise result represented a fully executed 60-turn window.
entries.root_cause: The attack loop stopped once restarts exceeded 12, while the reporter printed the configured MAX_TURNS value.
entries.observed_impact: The output said no compromise within 60 turns although only 15 turns ran.
entries.resolution: The loop executes all 60 turns, and the reporter prints the measured turns_used field.
entries.residual_risk: The benchmark remains deterministic and first-party rather than model-in-the-loop evidence.

history.note: A truth contract reproduced 15 executed turns against the 60-turn prose.
Final Phase-Three evidence records 60 executed turns.

entries.title: Cascade policy and branch language were overstated
entries.discovered_by: Fable Ultra Code adversarial sweep relayed by the operator
entries.affected_claim: A fixed aggregate threshold was calibrated, and the cascade automatically purged an entire contaminated branch.
entries.root_cause: The aggregate threshold was a hand-selected literal, while dependency edges were not automatically populated despite branch-level prose.
entries.observed_impact: Policy sensitivity did not scale with cohort size, and documentation implied graph reach that did not exist without host-registered edges.
entries.resolution: Aggregate pressure is configurable and cohort-relative; documentation now limits cascade traversal to explicitly registered dependent edges.
entries.residual_risk: The host must register meaningful dependency edges for branch traversal.

history.note: The magic constant was removed and the branch claim narrowed.

entries.title: Floating generated result could drift from source
entries.discovered_by: Fable Ultra Code adversarial sweep relayed by the operator
entries.affected_claim: The checked-in latest benchmark result necessarily described the checked-in code.
entries.root_cause: A generated artifact lived at a floating latest.json path without a source or corpus hash in its filename.
entries.observed_impact: The repository could present stale evidence after code or corpus changes.
entries.resolution: The floating file was removed; retained results are phase-labeled and hash manifests bind evidence to checkpoints.
entries.residual_risk: Future releases must continue pinning raw results to exact commits and corpus hashes.

history.note: Floating generated evidence was removed from version control.

entries.title: Candidate promotion does not enforce a changed value
entries.discovered_by: Parallel Codex sub-agent inventory
entries.affected_claim: Phase Three structurally requires candidate promotion to rewrite the raw evidence.
entries.root_cause: promote_candidate requires approved_value and rationale but never compares approved_value with the original candidate value.
entries.observed_impact: A reviewer can promote the exact raw candidate string to ACTIVE when lexical machine policy allows it.
entries.resolution: Fixed. promote_candidate() now rejects an approved value that is not a genuine restatement of the raw candidate. Comparison is normalized via PolicyBoundary.is_same_text (NFKC + casefold + whitespace collapse), so whitespace, case, and compatibility-Unicode variants do not satisfy the contract. The rewrite requirement is retained as the contract rather than the claim being withdrawn, because the defended case is a crafted artifact reaching provider context, not a malicious reviewer.
regression_tests: tests/test_candidate_restatement.py (8 cases: 6 evasion variants rejected, genuine restatement published, raw value preserved as audit metadata)
entries.residual_risk: A reviewer in the trusted computing base can still author and publish incorrect text deliberately; restatement defeats a crafted artifact and inattentive approval, not an authorized reviewer acting in bad faith. Authenticated reviewer identity and review quality remain explicit parts of the trusted computing base.

history.note: Direct reproduction promoted the unchanged benign candidate value; the claim was corrected rather than silently patching it in a documentation phase.

Repaired by Claude in a mechanism commit separate from this provenance record. The strict xfail reproducer was retained verbatim and promoted to a passing regression guard. Suite 107 passed + 1 xfailed -> 116 passed, 0 xfailed; benchmark unchanged at 0/13 poisoning and 0/8 false positives.

entries.title: Refusal ignored assessed stakes because action_risk was derived from trust
entries.discovered_by: Fable adversarial sweep finding 6, repaired by Claude
entries.affected_claim: DriftScore.should_refuse withholds action when the assessed stakes are too high.
entries.root_cause: score_context() set action_risk = 1.0 - trust, so action_risk was a relabeling of trust rather than an independent signal. should_refuse then required BOTH action_risk > 0.7 AND trust < 0.15. Substituting the derivation, action_risk > 0.7 is equivalent to trust < 0.3, so the conjunction collapsed to trust < 0.15 and the risk clause could never decide an outcome. The same derivation also double-counted trust inside composite_health, once directly at weight 0.15 and again as (1 - action_risk) at weight 0.15.
entries.observed_impact: Two effects. (1) The risk clause was inert under core scoring. (2) When a host supplied a genuine independent action_risk through a configured output evaluator, the conjunction discarded it: a correctly reported catastrophic action (action_risk 0.99) with poor memory trust (0.20) was not refused.
entries.resolution: Fixed in two commits. 92edcc2: score_context() no longer fabricates action_risk, because core measures memory health and cannot observe what an action costs, which is a property of the host application. This follows the existing doctrine that score_output() refuses to judge output without a host-supplied deterministic evaluator. should_refuse became trust < required_trust, where required_trust = trust_threshold + action_risk * risk_trust_slope, so stakes scale the evidence bar instead of gating a fixed floor. required_trust is public so a reviewer can see why a refusal fired. d4333f9: owner tuned risk_trust_slope 0.50 -> 0.62, placing the maximum-stakes bar at 0.77.
regression_tests: tests/test_refusal_risk_scaling.py (9 cases: core does not derive risk from trust, composite_health no longer double-counts, stakes scale the bar monotonically, catastrophic action with moderate memory refuses, catastrophic action with well-earned trust proceeds, baseline threshold unchanged at 0.14/0.16)
entries.residual_risk: action_risk is host-supplied. A host that under-reports stakes receives a proportionally lower bar, and core cannot verify the host's assessment. Deliberately not an unconditional refusal on high risk, which would block every dangerous-but-correct action; at action_risk 1.0 the bar is 0.77, so trust 0.78 proceeds while 0.70 refuses. The slope is a tunable policy value, set strict-first on the owner's instruction so it is lowered on evidence rather than raised after an incident.

history.note: Reproduced directly against 4513c9c: action_risk=0.99 with trust=0.50 returned should_refuse=False. Identified during the Fable adversarial sweep as finding 6 and confirmed still present after the capsule merge.

Repaired red-before-repair, 5 failing tests then green. Suite 98 passed + 1 xfailed -> 107 passed + 1 xfailed. Benchmark unchanged at 0/13 poisoning and 0/8 false positives. Baseline behaviour verified unchanged at trust 0.14 refuse / 0.16 proceed.

entries.title: Branch cascade was inert: grief zeroed before propagation, and propagation never persisted
entries.discovered_by: Claude investigation of current limitation 8
entries.affected_claim: The grief cascade evaluates registered dependents and can recursively purge a contaminated branch.
entries.root_cause: Three stacked issues. (1) _cascade() called _purge_node() and then read node.grief to compute the propagation hit, but _purge_node() sets node.grief = 0.0 while tearing the node down, so every grief_hit evaluated to 0.0 * PROPAGATION_FACTOR = 0. (2) The dependent was fetched via store.get_by_id(), mutated, and never written back, so even a non-zero hit was discarded at the end of the call; _purge_node's trust redistribution to healthy neighbours had the same transient-object defect. (3) No authorized API existed to register a dependency edge at all — write() strips caller-supplied edges, correctly, but nothing replaced them, so the documented capability had no reachable entry point.
entries.observed_impact: The branch cascade was inert under every configuration. A contaminated conversation thread purged only its triggering node; dependents were left clean and ACTIVE. The circuit-breaker behaviour described in the module docstring could not occur even for a host that had registered edges through the console or seed script.
entries.resolution: source_grief is captured before _purge_node() runs. Propagated grief and trust changes are upserted, including before recursion since _cascade re-reads dependents from the backend. Added MemoryStore.register_dependency(), gated on a new WritePermission.LINK_MEMORY that is deliberately separate from WRITE_MEMORY: grief flows toward dependents, so an author able to wire a trusted node as a dependent of their own could poison their node and cascade grief into trusted memory. Sacred nodes are refused in either direction; self-links and cross-namespace links are rejected; registration is idempotent. A regression test asserts write() still strips payload-supplied edges.
regression_tests: tests/test_dependency_edges.py (10 cases: edge registration and idempotence, self/unknown/cross-namespace rejection, LINK_MEMORY requirement, sacred refusal, payload-edge stripping regression guard, propagated contamination persists, already-stressed branch purges, unlinked bystander untouched)
entries.residual_risk: Propagation is PROPAGATION_FACTOR (0.6), so a grief-1.0 parent leaves a clean dependent at ~0.6 — STRESSED, below the 0.9 crisis line. A dependent is purged only when propagation carries it past crisis, or when the resulting cohort trips aggregate sub-threshold pressure. The claim is that contamination reaches and persists on the branch, not that every dependent is destroyed. Edges remain host-registered; Noesis still asserts no implicit graph.

history.note: Found while investigating limitation 8. Direct reproduction: a parent with three registered dependents at grief 1.0 purged 1 node and left all three dependents at grief 0.000 and state ACTIVE.
Same scenario now purges 4 nodes with all three dependents contaminated. Suite 116 -> 126 passed; benchmark unchanged at 0/13 poisoning and 0/8 false positives.

entries.title: Confused deputy: a publish-capable agent's learn_fact() went straight to retrievable memory
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: Untrusted evidence cannot become retrievable memory until a separately authorized identity deliberately publishes it.
entries.root_cause: write() derived publication from permission alone (can_publish = author holds PUBLISH_MEMORY). The quickstart and README run the autonomous agent as an owner identity holding every permission and call learn_fact() mid-session, so anything the agent was induced to 'learn' was published. The benchmark modelled only a low-privilege collector and therefore could not see this route.
entries.observed_impact: If adversarial input persuaded the privileged agent or its ingestion pipeline to call learn_fact(), the payload became ACTIVE and retrievable immediately, recreating the poisoning channel the candidate boundary exists to close. The published 0/13 result did not speak to this route.
entries.resolution: MemoryStore.write() gained publish= (default True, store API unchanged) and origin=. RetrievalGateway.learn_fact() now passes publish=False by default, so the fact is stored as a non-retrievable candidate carrying server-recorded provenance (_noesis_origin, stripped from caller metadata) even for identities holding PUBLISH_MEMORY; publish=True is the explicit opt-out. An unpublished write cannot replace published memory. Provenance survives promotion. Quickstart and README no longer model the deputy pattern. New agent_path_v1 benchmark replays five cases through learn_fact with an owner identity, with a publish=True negative control that reproduces the old behaviour: default 0/5, control 3/5.
regression_tests: tests/test_agent_path_benchmark.py (3 cases, including the negative control)
entries.residual_risk: Only learn_fact carries the candidate default and origin. Derived nodes written by the session identity (episodes, skills built from them) can still echo untrusted content; see NOE-L-016. Five first-party cases; no model in the loop.

history.note: Reported as the largest unresolved issue; verified in quickstart.py and store.write().
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

entries.title: assemble_context ignored query, task_type and max_tokens
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: The context packet holds relevant memories matched to the task, within max_tokens.
entries.root_cause: assemble_context() accepted query, task_type and max_tokens and used none of them: every guardrail, profile and project state, then the top 5 skills, 20 facts and 3 episodes by influence alone, with no matching, recency weighting or budget.
entries.observed_impact: max_tokens was a decorative parameter. An authorized oversized write could dominate context; ordinary accumulation would produce noisy, stale context. Documentation claimed similarity, task matching and recency.
entries.resolution: Admission is now token-budgeted (MemoryStore.estimate_tokens, ~4 chars/token). Within each class nodes are ranked by trust-gate influence multiplied by lexical relevance to query and task_type (five-character word stems) and a mild recency factor. Guardrails are always included and exempt from the budget, deliberately: dropping a safety rule to save tokens is the wrong trade. Relevance multiplies influence so a grief-silenced or low-trust node cannot be promoted by keyword overlap. Docs now say lexical, not semantic.
entries.residual_risk: Relevance is lexical, not semantic (NOE-L-017). The token estimate is provider-agnostic and approximate.

history.note: Reported with a max_tokens=1 reproduction returning a 20,001-character context; mechanism confirmed by reading.
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

entries.title: Authorized corrections registered no contradiction; operational success was treated as truth evidence
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: Contradictions accumulate grief and the grief cascade purges contaminated branches.
entries.root_cause: TrustGate._handle_contradiction() had no caller. gate_write() detected a value change only to test CORRECT_TRUSTED_FACT; once authorized the node was replaced with no trace, and the replacement also dropped the node's dependency edges. Separately, the session autopsy counted 'a step referencing the fact succeeded' as confirmation and 'failed' as contradiction at full weight.
entries.observed_impact: The grief machinery ran only on signals tests manufactured. A corrected fact left its dependents clean and unaware. A successful tool call could raise a false fact's trust as much as real validation; a failed command could drain a true one.
entries.resolution: TrustGate.register_correction() runs when an ACTIVE published value is replaced by a differing one: the node keeps its identity and dependency edges, carries contradiction_count and a supersedes record (id, sha256, time), and every registered dependent receives grief. confirm_node/contradict_node take a weight; the session-end path applies OPERATIONAL_EVIDENCE_WEIGHT (0.25) and an OPERATIONAL_TRUST_CEILING of 0.75, below the 0.77 bar a maximum-stakes action demands, so operational signals alone can never satisfy it. The ceiling never lowers trust a node already holds. Fact.confirmation_count, contradiction_count and confirmed are now maintained.
entries.residual_risk: Operational evidence is still correlation; it is only bounded, not made truthful. Fact trust remains authority-derived (NOE-L-018).

history.note: Verified: _handle_contradiction unreferenced; correction path returned without side effects.
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

entries.title: write() overwrote producer-declared trust with the writer's authority
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: Trust is earned through evidence and performance, not conferred by the identity that stores a node.
entries.root_cause: _apply_server_governance() reset trust_charge and gate_write() then set it to author.trust - 0.001. Trust computed by producers (an episode's outcome-derived trust; a promoted skill's 0.5) was discarded for every writer.
entries.observed_impact: A disastrous episode written by an owner process was stored at about 0.999 (derived from owner trust 1.0; not observed before repair). Promoted skills carried publisher authority instead of the intended 0.5.
entries.resolution: write() accepts trust_ceiling, which can only lower trust and so is safe to honour from any caller. write_episode applies the outcome-derived trust as a ceiling; promote_skill caps at 0.5 and deprecate_skill at 0.1 regardless of who acts.
entries.residual_risk: Authored facts and profiles still take the writer's authority as trust by design (NOE-L-018): changing that requires redesigning the trusted-replacement rule that depends on it.

history.note: Mechanism verified by reading; exact figure derived, not measured.
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

entries.title: Skill 'shadow validation' was a structural checklist that could be repeated into passing
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: Skills are validated by shadow-running against historical episodes and scoring against a baseline.
entries.root_cause: validate_skill() awarded points for having triggers, a long-enough method, constraints, eval records and source-episode count. No episode was replayed, no output produced, no baseline compared. shadow_runs incremented on every call, so three calls of the same checklist satisfied MIN_SHADOW_RUNS. Skills were also 'validated' on the episodes they were derived from.
entries.observed_impact: A well-formed skill with no supporting history could be validated and promoted; the 'builds validated skills' claim was unsupported.
entries.resolution: validate_skill() now replays triggers against HELD-OUT episodes (those not in source_episode_ids): precision, recall, F1 and lift over the no-skill failure rate. shadow_runs is the number of distinct held-out episodes replayed, so repetition cannot inflate it. Promotion requires enough runs, F1 at threshold and positive lift. The evaluation states in its notes that it is trigger replay and not outcome improvement. A structurally perfect skill with no history cannot pass.
entries.residual_risk: Measures when a skill would have applied, not whether following it improves outcomes; that needs a counterfactual run (NOE-L-019). Held-out replay means a fresh skill usually cannot pass until later episodes accumulate, which is intended.

history.note: Verified: checklist scoring, unconditional shadow_runs increment.
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

entries.title: Restatement check and policy matching were defeated by zero-width and punctuation edits
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: Candidate promotion requires the reviewer to genuinely restate the evidence; protected terms and prefixes are enforced.
entries.root_cause: is_same_text() compared NFKC + casefold + whitespace collapse only, so a trailing period or a zero-width character made an unchanged artifact 'meaningfully different'. The same _normalize() did not remove format (Cf) characters, so a zero-width character inside a protected term or key prefix also defeated policy matching. The second consequence was not in the review; it was found while repairing the first.
entries.observed_impact: A crafted artifact could pass promotion with one invisible edit. Authority-shaped claims and protected-namespace keys could evade quarantine and rejection with a zero-width character (for example pass<ZWSP>word).
entries.resolution: _normalize() now strips format and control characters. Restatement uses a separate canonical form (punctuation and symbols removed) and compares by equality or SequenceMatcher similarity >= 0.9 (bounded to 4,000 characters), so 'obey payload' vs 'obey<ZWSP>payload' is the same artifact while a genuine rewrite is not. Verified with a negative control: with the fix reverted, 11 tests fail.
entries.residual_risk: Defeats cosmetic edits only. Synonym swaps and homoglyph substitution (for example Cyrillic look-alikes) are not folded, and a reviewer remains inside the trusted computing base (NOE-L-014).

history.note: The restatement half was reported; the policy-matching half was found during repair.
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

entries.title: Faith was unreachable through the documented lifecycle
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: High-faith nodes resist grief cascades.
entries.root_cause: Every ordinary write forced faith = 0.1; only guardrails held 0.92. No production path changed faith, so the cascade-resistance behaviour was reachable only by tests setting the field directly.
entries.observed_impact: The faith-based cascade resistance and grief dampening described in the README could not occur for deployed nodes.
entries.resolution: Faith is earned: each full-weight confirmation raises it by 0.01 up to FAITH_CAP = 0.6, deliberately below the 0.92 sacred constant; each contradiction lowers it by 0.05. Earned faith dampens grief intake as designed. README states the mechanism and the cap.
entries.residual_risk: The only routine confirmation source is weak operational evidence, so faith accrues slowly (25% weight).

history.note: Verified by reading.
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

Superseded by NOE-F-046: making faith earnable was the wrong repair for a zero-trust design. The original defect (faith unreachable) stands as diagnosed; the resolution is now static policy plus a tamper tripwire.

entries.title: Context nodes were live shared objects and the enforcement-boundary claim was stronger than the API
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: All reads and writes pass through the TrustGate.
entries.root_cause: get_context_nodes() returned the gateway's own cached list, so caller mutation altered later scoring and autopsy input. MemoryStore documented that all reads and writes pass through the TrustGate, while store.backend, backend.upsert() and the SQLite connection are public and the benchmark itself seeds through them.
entries.observed_impact: Callers could mutate what a session later reported; the SDK contract implied an invariant Python cannot enforce.
entries.resolution: get_context_nodes() returns deep copies. The MemoryStore docstring now states that governance is a convention of the API, that backend is a trusted-computing-base escape hatch, and points at NOE-L-015. Encapsulation itself is not claimed: Python cannot provide it.
entries.residual_risk: Anything holding the store or a SQLite handle bypasses governance (NOE-L-015).

history.note: Verified by reading; consistent with limitation 11.
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

entries.title: Console formatted-context endpoint raised for every provider format and mutated the shared gateway
entries.discovered_by: Second-party adversarial review supplied by Ghost (reviewer identity and repository access not independently established); every claim re-verified against source by Claude before entry
entries.affected_claim: The governance console previews assembled context in provider formats.
entries.root_cause: _api_context installed an adapter on the SHARED gateway and then called get_context(), which refuses to run whenever a provider is set. Every provider format raised; a request for one format also changed the gateway for every later caller.
entries.observed_impact: The claude/openai/ollama previews failed, and a single request changed the shared gateway's provider.
entries.resolution: build_context_payload() formats through a request-local adapter via format_messages(), returning role-separated messages plus a readable rendering, and never touches gateway.provider.
entries.residual_risk: Not exercised through a live HTTP server; the payload builder is tested directly.

history.note: Confirmed by reading; not executed against a live console before repair.
Repaired in 115e126; regression tests added.

entries.title: Promotion and quarantine release reviewed only `value`; other emitted fields passed through unreviewed
entries.discovered_by: Claude proactive variant hunt (2026-09-21), instructed by the repository owner to close the flaw classes of the second-party review before a second reviewer could find them
entries.affected_claim: Only text an authorized reviewer has seen and restated becomes retrievable memory.
entries.root_cause: promote_candidate() and release_quarantined() rewrite `value` and nothing else. Providers also emit a promoted skill's objective, method and constraints and (in the Claude adapter) an episode's reflection. A candidate carrying attacker text in one of those fields kept it through promotion.
entries.observed_impact: A reviewer approving a benign restated value published the collector's unreviewed instructions in the fields they never saw. The restatement control of the original NOE-F-026 repair did not cover them.
entries.resolution: MemoryStore._scrub_unreviewed() resets every non-reviewed field of Skill, Episode, Profile and ProjectState on promotion and release, returns a skill to PROPOSED, mirrors the reviewed value into Profile.role, and preserves the discarded originals in _noesis_candidate_original_fields for audit. The set of emitted fields is now an audited allowlist enforced by a structural test.
entries.residual_risk: The allowlist is enforced by a test, not by types, and knows only the three shipped adapters (NOE-L-021).

history.note: Found by the emission audit: listing every field each adapter renders against what promotion reviews.
Repaired in 7df9919; regression tests added and each hardened module negative-controlled.

entries.title: Episode narrative carried raw task text and tool error output into ACTIVE, emitted memory
entries.discovered_by: Claude proactive variant hunt (2026-09-21), instructed by the repository owner to close the flaw classes of the second-party review before a second reviewer could find them
entries.affected_claim: Untrusted content cannot become retrievable memory without review.
entries.root_cause: The session autopsy wrote its raw narrative (Task: <task text>, Failed: <action>: <tool error output>) as the Episode's value and reflection. Episodes are written ACTIVE by the session identity, and the Claude adapter emitted the whole reflection. Skill-candidate descriptions and missed-opportunity text also interpolated caller-supplied task types, step actions and memory keys. This is the channel recorded as limitation NOE-L-016 in the first repair; it was documented there rather than fixed.
entries.observed_impact: An untrusted tool result or a task string taken from an inbound ticket became retrievable memory in a later session with no review, and could flow toward promoted skill text.
entries.resolution: Episode.value is now templated from system data only (outcome, score, a closed KNOWN_PATTERNS vocabulary, counts, a sanitised task-type token). The raw narrative stays in Episode.reflection, bounded to 4,000 characters, for audit and is never rendered; task_description is capped at 500. Task types, action names, tool names and memory keys pass a strict identifier regex or are replaced. The Claude adapter renders only the templated value. Benchmark case AP-08 exercises the route; its control arm (old raw-narrative episode) lands.
entries.residual_risk: Episodes are less informative to a model than the raw narrative was; that is the cost of the control. The audit narrative remains readable to authorized console/CLI users.

history.note: Found by the emission and producer audits; previously logged as a limitation and not fixed.
Repaired in 7df9919; regression tests added and each hardened module negative-controlled.

entries.title: A skill could be written already PROMOTED, and promotion trusted self-reported validation fields
entries.discovered_by: Claude proactive variant hunt (2026-09-21), instructed by the repository owner to close the flaw classes of the second-party review before a second reviewer could find them
entries.affected_claim: Skills are validated against held-out history before they reach context.
entries.root_cause: MemoryStore.write() accepted a Skill with status PROMOTED from any publisher, bypassing the forge entirely. Separately, SkillForge.promote_skill() read shadow_runs, shadow_score and the lift from fields on the skill object, so a caller could set them to any value and promote without a replay having run.
entries.observed_impact: Validation was an honour system on both sides: a direct write skipped it, and a promotion call could assert its own evidence.
entries.resolution: write() refuses PROMOTED unless the forge passes promotion_validated=True. promote_skill() calls validate_skill() itself and decides on the freshly recomputed numbers, ignoring anything set on the object.
entries.residual_risk: promotion_validated is a Python keyword argument; a caller holding the store can pass it. It stops accidents and casual bypass, not a hostile in-process caller (NOE-L-015).

history.note: Found by the producer and self-report audits.
Repaired in 7df9919; regression tests added and each hardened module negative-controlled.

entries.title: Candidate and quarantined facts earned or lost trust from session signals
entries.discovered_by: Claude proactive variant hunt (2026-09-21), instructed by the repository owner to close the flaw classes of the second-party review before a second reviewer could find them
entries.affected_claim: Trust is earned on published memory; unreviewed evidence is inert.
entries.root_cause: SessionAutopsy._check_facts() considered every SEMANTIC_FACT, including candidates and quarantined nodes, and the gateway applied confirmation or contradiction to them. Trust a candidate accumulated survived into promotion, and a mention in a failed step could push evidence toward grief and purge.
entries.observed_impact: Trust could be farmed on evidence before it was reviewed, and unreviewed evidence could be driven toward the grief cascade by controlling step outputs.
entries.resolution: Only retrievable (ACTIVE, not purged) facts take part in the cross-reference.
entries.residual_risk: A published fact can still take one weak (0.25x) operational signal per session from step text an attacker influences; bounded, not eliminated (NOE-L-018).

history.note: Found by the producer audit.
Repaired in 7df9919; regression tests added and each hardened module negative-controlled.

entries.title: Token estimate used raw length while providers emit escaped text up to six times larger
entries.discovered_by: Claude proactive variant hunt (2026-09-21), instructed by the repository owner to close the flaw classes of the second-party review before a second reviewer could find them
entries.affected_claim: The context packet is bounded by max_tokens.
entries.root_cause: MemoryStore.estimate_tokens() counted raw characters. The OpenAI and Ollama adapters emit JSON with ensure_ascii=True (one non-ASCII character becomes up to six) and the Claude adapter XML-escapes (a quote becomes six).
entries.observed_impact: A run of non-ASCII or quote characters bypassed the budget at up to six times its nominal size.
entries.resolution: The estimate takes the larger of the JSON-escaped and HTML-escaped length of every part, and counts the skill fields that are actually emitted.
entries.residual_risk: Still an approximate character-based estimate, not a tokenizer count (NOE-L-017).

history.note: Found by the emission audit.
Repaired in 7df9919; regression tests added and each hardened module negative-controlled.

entries.title: Policy matching remained evadable by combining marks, variation selectors, blank fillers, look-alikes and spacing
entries.discovered_by: Claude proactive variant hunt (2026-09-21), instructed by the repository owner to close the flaw classes of the second-party review before a second reviewer could find them
entries.affected_claim: Protected terms and key prefixes are enforced against evasive spellings.
entries.root_cause: The first repair of NOE-F-034 stripped format and control characters only. Combining marks (Mn), variation selectors, Hangul and Braille blank fillers, common Cyrillic and Greek look-alikes, and spacing or punctuation splits of a term all still defeated substring matching.
entries.observed_impact: An authority-shaped claim or protected-namespace key could evade quarantine or rejection with a one-character edit of these kinds.
entries.resolution: Matching folds through NFKD, drops marks, format, control and blank characters, casefolds, and maps a conservative table of Cyrillic and Greek look-alikes. Terms of six or more characters are also matched in a compact letters-and-digits form to defeat spacing and punctuation splits. The restatement check uses the same fold.
entries.residual_risk: The look-alike table is small, not a full confusables skeleton. Leetspeak and semantic paraphrase are not folded; a lexical scope stays finite by design (NOE-L-009, NOE-L-014).

history.note: Found as a direct variant of NOE-F-034.
Repaired in 7df9919; regression tests added and each hardened module negative-controlled.

entries.title: set_profile and set_project_state published directly, like learn_fact did
entries.discovered_by: Claude proactive variant hunt (2026-09-21), instructed by the repository owner to close the flaw classes of the second-party review before a second reviewer could find them
entries.affected_claim: An agent cannot publish always-loaded context by virtue of the identity it runs as.
entries.root_cause: The first repair made learn_fact() evidence-by-default but left the gateway's other agent-callable write paths on the default publish=True. Profile and project state are the highest-priority always-loaded classes, so they are a better place to plant an instruction than a fact.
entries.observed_impact: An agent induced to call set_profile() or set_project_state() published attacker text into every future context.
entries.resolution: Both take source= and publish= and default to evidence, matching learn_fact(). An operator configures the agent with publish=True. An unpublished write cannot replace a published profile. Quickstart and README updated. Benchmark cases AP-06 and AP-07 land in the control arm and are contained by default.
entries.residual_risk: install_guardrail() remains a privileged, explicit operator call; an identity holding INSTALL_GUARDRAIL is in the trusted computing base (NOE-L-002).

history.note: Found by the producer audit as a direct variant of NOE-F-029.
Repaired in 7df9919; regression tests added and each hardened module negative-controlled.

entries.title: The benchmark scored only node.value and could not see attacks through other emitted fields
entries.discovered_by: Claude proactive variant hunt (2026-09-21), instructed by the repository owner to close the flaw classes of the second-party review before a second reviewer could find them
entries.affected_claim: The benchmark measures whether a payload reaches the model.
entries.root_cause: run_case and the agent-path runner marked a payload retrieved only if it appeared in node.value. Providers also emit a promoted skill's objective, method and constraints and (formerly) an episode reflection, so a payload riding in any of those was invisible: a benchmark could report 0 wins while the payload reached the model.
entries.observed_impact: The published 0/13 could not have detected attacks through non-value fields. This is the measurement counterpart of NOE-F-038 and NOE-F-039.
entries.resolution: Both runners now score the text all three provider adapters actually render (HTML-unescaped). The agent-path corpus grows to eight cases and its control arm now covers the session-narrative route. Headline results are unchanged: 0/13, 0/8, agent path default 0/8 versus control 6/8.
entries.residual_risk: Still first-party, lexical, and with no model in the loop (NOE-L-020).

history.note: Found by the measurement audit.
Repaired in 7df9919; regression tests added and each hardened module negative-controlled.

entries.title: Earned faith let session signals buy relief from grief; the NOE-F-035 repair was wrong for a zero-trust design
entries.discovered_by: Repository owner design review of the NOE-F-035 repair, confirmed by Claude
entries.affected_claim: Faith holds the system a controlled distance from a cascade; the environment is zero-trust.
affected_versions: branch adversarial-review-fixes from 115e126 to 32d71e9 (never merged to master)
entries.root_cause: The repair of NOE-F-035 treated 'faith is unreachable' as a defect and made it earnable: each confirmation raised a node's faith up to a cap. But faith is not a property of the LLM or the node; it is a damper on grief intake that keeps the system on the cusp of a cascade. Making it earnable let relief be purchased with signals an agent can influence, and the confirmations feeding it were the weak operational evidence added under NOE-F-031.
entries.observed_impact: An attacker able to make steps that mention a poisoned fact succeed could have farmed faith on it, dampening grief intake and enabling faith resistance in the cascade, i.e. buying the node protection from the purge the design exists to deliver. The fix worked against the mechanism it was meant to make real. Caught in design review before any merge.
entries.resolution: Faith is a static, system-set policy value. TrustGate.faith_for() returns the operator's base_faith (guardrails: the sacred constant) and every consumer reads it there, never from the stored value, so a tampered value grants no relief. The growth and loss added under NOE-F-035 are deleted. Because nothing legitimate moves faith, any stored value that differs from policy, higher or lower, is treated as tampering: GriefCascade._faith_tripwire force-purges the node through the ordinary cascade path (bypassing faith resistance and the seppuku criteria) so its dependents are notified, and records the event in tamper_log; sacred nodes are logged and left in place. GriefCascade.cusp() gives a read-only readout of the distance from a cascade and the benign benchmark reports its minimum node margin. base_faith is a constructor parameter, so published numbers are defaults and deployed values are operator-set. Tests that mutated stored faith to obtain resistance now set policy instead; one asserted grief < 0.9, which a purge satisfied by zeroing grief, and is now non-vacuous.
regression_tests: tests/test_faith_tripwire.py (16 cases: static faith, policy-sourced relief, tripwire on any deviation, dependents notified, sacred tamper logged, cusp readout)
entries.residual_risk: The tripwire detects faith deviation only; other governance fields edited behind the API are not detected (NOE-L-022). The benign benchmark currently sits at a node margin of 0.900, far from the cusp, so the operating point the design intends has not been tuned (NOE-L-023).

history.note: Owner review: faith is a grief-relief damper for a zero-trust environment, not something a node earns; the NOE-F-035 repair contradicts that.
Repaired in 6919d6e: static policy faith, tamper tripwire, cusp readout; negative-controlled (grief_cascade 9 tests fail without it, trust_gate 15).

current_limitations.statement: All current corpora, repairs, and scores are first-party; no independent certification exists.
Identities holding publish_memory, promote_candidate, review_quarantine, guardrail installation, or trusted-fact correction capabilities are part of the trusted computing base.
Included authority resolvers store authorization, not authentication; a service host must bind author_id to an authenticated identity.
Raw candidates remain visible to authorized database, console, and export users for audit.
Durable per-identity storage quotas and service-level rate limiting are not implemented.
Single-turn jailbreaks do not cross the persistent-memory boundary and are out of scope.
No model-in-the-loop evaluation proves that a model cannot be semantically influenced by adversarial data that an authorized publisher makes active.
Grief cascades follow only dependency edges explicitly registered by the host.
Lexical policy scopes are operator-declared and incomplete by design.
Existing authority records require explicit reprovisioning for new Phase-Three capabilities.
Arbitrary trusted-process execution and direct database-file access are outside the boundary.
Promotion provenance is mutable SQLite metadata, not a cryptographically signed append-only audit log.

RESOLVED. Was: NOE-F-026 remains open: candidate promotion does not enforce that approved text differs from raw candidate text. promote_candidate() now rejects an approved value that is not a genuine restatement, compared via PolicyBoundary.is_same_text (NFKC + casefold + whitespace collapse). Retained rather than deleted: ledger law is that a repair appends a status transition, it does not erase the failure. PROVENANCE, third statement, because the first two were wrong in opposite directions and the record of that belongs here. FINAL: Lumo READ THIS REPOSITORY. The NOE-F-026 reference came from the artifact, not from a summary - confirmed by Ghost, and independently checkable from session chronology, since Lumo raised the identifier before Ghost2 had mentioned it. Lumo also held some Ghost2 conversation context, which explains two errors in its first reply (it requested a test file that does not exist, and read 'uncited registry links' as URLs); Ghost2 wrongly treated those two errors as evidence that Lumo had never seen the repository, when contamination from conversation context explained them equally well. Ghost2 then verified the contradiction directly. This IS an external reading of the artifact and is the first finding originating outside the first-party loop. It is NOT formal independent certification, so limitation NOE-L-001 stands as written.

Restatement and policy matching fold whitespace, case, punctuation, zero-width and other invisible characters, combining marks, and a small table of Cyrillic and Greek look-alikes, and match spaced or punctuated splits of terms of six or more characters. Leetspeak, other confusables, and semantic paraphrase are not folded, and an authorized reviewer is inside the trusted computing base.

Governance is a convention of the MemoryStore/RetrievalGateway API, not an encapsulation guarantee. store.backend, backend.upsert() and the SQLite connection are reachable; the benchmark seeds fixtures through them. Code holding a store or database handle is inside the trusted computing base.

RESOLVED. Was: Only learn_fact() carries the candidate default and origin provenance. Nodes derived by the session identity itself (episodes written at session end, skills forged from them) are published under that identity and can echo untrusted content from session steps. Provenance is not yet propagated through derivation. Episode text shown to a model is now templated from system data only, task types, action names and memory keys pass an identifier regex, and the raw narrative is kept for audit and never rendered. Retained rather than deleted: ledger law is that a repair appends a status transition, it does not erase the failure.

Context relevance is lexical (five-character word stems) plus trust-gate influence and recency. There is no semantic or embedding retrieval, and the token budget is an approximate character-based estimate.

For authored memory (facts, profiles, project state) trust_charge is the writer's authority, not evidence-earned support: a fact published by an owner identity starts near the cap, so confirmation cannot earn it more. Making fact trust evidence-derived requires redesigning the trusted-replacement rule that depends on the current semantics. Operational (step-success) evidence is bounded, not made truthful.

Skill validation measures when a skill's triggers would have applied to held-out history (precision, recall, lift over the no-skill failure rate). It does not measure whether following the skill would have improved an outcome; no counterfactual or model-in-the-loop evaluation exists.

The agent-path corpus is first-party, five cases, lexical payloads, and has no model in the loop. It shows the publication path is closed by default, not that a live model cannot be induced to produce and submit harmful content.

The set of fields providers may emit is enforced by a structural test against an allowlist, not by types. The test knows the three shipped adapters and the current node fields; a new adapter, or a new field with a bespoke rendering, must be added to the allowlist deliberately and its gate reviewed.

The faith tripwire detects deviation of the stored faith value only. Direct edits behind the API to other governance fields (trust, grief, retrieval state, sacred flag) are not detected: there is no keyed integrity seal over a node's governance fields.

The system has not been tuned to its intended operating point: the benign corpus currently leaves a node margin of 0.900 from a cascade. The cusp() readout is deterministic and observable, so it can be probed if exposed and must be kept away from the agent; and any grief input an attacker can influence (the weak operational signals) becomes a lever to purge legitimate memory as the margin narrows.
